definition: Determining where and how a robot should grip an object, using visual and tactile cues — a core manipulation skill learned increasingly from data.
details: Determining where and how a robot should grip an object, using visual and tactile cues — a core manipulation skill learned increasingly from data.

explainer.lead: Robotic grasping is deciding where and how a robot should grip an object, using visual and tactile cues. It matters because grasping is a core manipulation skill and is increasingly learned from data.

tiers.eli5: It is a robot figuring out exactly where to put its fingers on a cup so it can pick it up without dropping or crushing it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine visual and tactile sensing and increasingly train grasp policies on data rather than hand-coding them. A pitfall is relying on vision alone when contact and slip need tactile feedback.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it maps object observations plus tactile cues to grasp poses and forces; learned approaches infer this from data. Known limit: performance depends on the coverage and quality of the training data and sensing.

explainer.example: A robot arm sees a mug, selects a grasp around the handle from visual cues, then uses tactile feedback to confirm grip before lifting.
